neighbours.label: the plural subject (patients, mice, babies, students) right after 'that' or a time phrase in a study finding
fire: The trial showed a high likelihood that patients given the drug would improve.
By six months of age, infants fed by bottle were more likely to be ill.
The sad part is that students who miss these classes drop out.
The team found that rats in the two groups ran more.
The data suggest that women from both towns improved.
By ten weeks, mice born in the cold were much smaller.
Reports indicate that children in rural areas read less.
The study found that nurses on night shifts slept less.
quiet: The trial showed a high likelihood that the drug would be approved.
By six months of age, the price of the bottle was much higher.
The sad part is that the classes were cancelled.
The team found that the room was warm.
The data suggest that the town improved its roads.
By ten weeks, the cold had passed.
Reports indicate that the rural road was closed.
The study found that the night shift was long.

short: plural subject in a study finding
notes: Direct logits promote ' that', ' who', ' younger'.
